title: You can honor a man…
paragraphs:
You can honor a man…
and still lose your soul.

Because not all deception looks like rebellion—
sometimes it looks like loyalty.
And that’s what makes it dangerous.

You didn’t wake up one day and decide to replace God.
No.

You admired a leader.
You were blessed by their words.
You saw God use them—and it was real.

Admiration became attachment.
Attachment became dependence.
Dependence became devotion.

Not away from church.
Not away from faith.
But away from Christ as the center.

Now your convictions rise and fall with a man’s voice.
Your peace depends on their approval.
Your theology echoes their opinions.

Anything that replaces Jesus…
even something “good”…
becomes an idol.

Because the same person who helped you encounter God…
can slowly become the filter through which you see Him.
But because they built their faith on a human foundation.
“Put not your trust in princes, in a son of man, in whom there is no salvation.” — Psalm 146:3

Not in charisma.
Not in gifting.
Not in influence.
Even the apostle Paul—used mightily by God—refused to take that place.
“Follow me, as I follow Christ.” — 1 Corinthians 11:1

That means the moment a leader drifts—
your loyalty doesn’t drift with them.

Some scholars interpret this as a safeguard against spiritual dependency—
a built-in protection so believers never confuse guidance with lordship.
Because pastors are called to point.
And here’s where it gets personal—
Some of you ignored red flags.
because you didn’t want to dishonor the leader.

And the enemy loves that kind of loyalty—
loyalty that refuses to test, refuses to discern, refuses to return to Scripture.
Because once your loyalty is misplaced—
It exposes what you built your faith on.
This is not just about leaders.
This is about the human heart.
Because we crave something we can see.
Someone who sounds confident, looks strong, feels certain.
But faith was never meant to rest on visible strength.
“We walk by faith, not by sight.” — 2 Corinthians 5:7

We elevate voices.
We idolize platforms.
We measure truth by popularity.

we trade intimacy with Jesus
for proximity to influence.

Because even if you’ve misplaced your loyalty—
even if you’ve followed a man more than Christ—
even if your faith feels shaken right now—
Jesus is not offended by your return.

Not that leaders are perfect.
Not that churches never fail.

But that you and I are sinners who needed saving—
not guidance alone, but redemption.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23

That includes pastors.
That includes you.
That includes me.
No one stands above the need for grace.
And that’s why no man can be your savior.
“But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
Jesus Christ lived the life we could not live, died the death we deserved, and rose again so we could be forgiven, restored, and made new.
And when your faith is built there—
it cannot be shaken by a man’s failure.

Not to a system.
Not to a personality.
Not to a platform.
Who has taken a place only Christ deserves?
Repent—not in shame, but in surrender.
Let Him be your center again.
Let Him be your authority again.
Let Him be your Savior again.
